column2: JUAN CARLOS LERENA and MARIA LERENA
column4: *** THE TWO THIS ARCHIVE EXISTS TO FIND, and the reason the red lane is drawn broken. *** They are named as the parents on Pablo Armando's army enrolment card and appear in NO OTHER RECORD ANYWHERE - not in Rosario, not in Montevideo, not in the full-text corpus. Every lane above is a candidate and none has been shown to hold them.

column2: The LARENA of Cayasta and Gualeguaychu
column4: Fourteen people in the register under the A-spelling (three of them wives of a Larena), in the two Argentine provinces either side of the Parana. *** THE SPELLING IS NOT THE PROBLEM - this archive has catalogued LERENA read as SERENA, LORENA, LESINA and six more. *** What is missing is any document joining them to a Uruguayan house.

Married ADELA CAMIGLIA; a son AVELINO CARLOS born 1904. *** The forename AVELINO is the one that runs through Sancho's house ***, which is suggestive and is not evidence. Worked in September and not joined.

column2: The LERENA of Trinidad with no father named
column4: CAYETANA FAUSTINA, whose son Luis was registered in 1895 with no father on the act; RODOLFO BERNARDO and ISMAEL, each a father who appears once. *** Real people on real acts, attached to nobody. ***

Four people, arrived together in 1889 - Anna, Annunziata, Laurensa, Savina. *** An Italian name that is not a spelling of this one ***, kept in the register so that nobody has to discover them twice. (The register also holds two Italian arrivals written LERENA, Domenico in 1910 and Paolo in 1913, who are unplaced and not excluded.)

Felipa, Pedro and Isidoro Lerena in the parish marriages of Chuquibamba, Condesuyos. *** Found while searching the full-text corpus and recorded because a rare name in a far place is exactly what a careless session would merge. ***
One full-text hit in the Colombian Catholic records. *** Not pursued and not ours. ***

column2: The LERENA y LERENA of Navarrete
column4: *** A WHOLE HOUSEHOLD WHO CARRY THE NAME TWICE, and the most useful namesake on this page. *** ISABELA LERENA y BASARAN, widow, of Navarrete in La Rioja; her sons JOSE DOLORES, married and the propietario at home, and PRUDENCIO BENITO and JUAN JOSE, bachelors and shop-assistants in Buenos Aires, who in November 1900 signed a power of attorney at the Spanish consulate putting the Spanish property in their mother's hands. *** WHY IT IS DRAWN HERE AND NOT ON A LANE: *** they are Spanish subjects out of Logrono, and the first two lanes above are Banda Oriental stock documented from the 1790s; the other three begin at Rosario, in Spain and in Spain, and no connection is claimed between this household and any of them. *** WHY IT IS DRAWN AT ALL: *** Pablo Armando's enrolment card names a JUAN CARLOS LERENA and a MARIA LERENA, and the easiest way to dismiss that card is to call the repeated surname a clerk's slip. *** AND THEY ARE THE SIXTH SUCH COUPLE THIS ARCHIVE HAS MET, NOT THE FIRST - a correction to what was written here first. *** The two Trinidad couples of 1894 and 1913, the 1911 dispensation, Alejandro, and Eloy x Felisa Lerena at San Jose de Flores in 1912 all came before them. *** SO THE CARD'S DOUBLE SURNAME WAS NEVER IN REAL DOUBT, AND NAVARRETE DOES NOT RESCUE IT. *** What Navarrete adds is different and smaller: it is the *** FIRST SUCH HOUSEHOLD OUTSIDE SOUTH AMERICA ***, the *** FIRST WHERE THE CHILDREN CARRY IT DOUBLED AS A SURNAME OF RECORD *** - 'Lerena y Lerena', in their own signatures, not just a coincidence of two parents - and the *** FIRST TIME THE PRACTICE HAS A PLACE ON A MAP *** that can be searched. It does not make them his - no connection is claimed, and the CEMLA arrivals suggest a steady traffic of young Riojan Lerena men into Buenos Aires shops that has nothing to do with Rosario de Santa Fe in 1882.

*** A Lerena household on the Brazilian border, found 12 October 2026 and not on any lane. *** Benito, b. about 1854, Oriental, a jornalero who could not sign his name; his wife Maria Cristina, b. about 1856, Brazilian, given no surname by the act; their daughter Anastasia LERENA, b. about 1877, married to the Brazilian soldier Honorio ALVAREZ. Artigas is a department this archive has never worked, and a family of the name sitting on the Brazil frontier with Brazilian-born children is a shape nothing here predicts. *** Found only because a LERENA father was asked against a SERENA mother - and the act turns out to say Lerena both times. ***

column3: Jesus Maria and Mal Abrigo, San Jose, Uruguay, 1910
column4: *** An Italian-born Lerena in the department this archive rests an 1846 couple on. *** Pedro, b. about 1842 in Italy, a labrador; Juana Camacho, b. about 1853, Oriental; their daughter Ramona LERENA, b. about 1886, who registered a natural daughter Antonina at Mal Abrigo in September 1910 with the father's line left as se ignora. *** Kept here rather than on a lane, and kept as UNPLACED rather than as a namesake, because the honest position is that this archive cannot yet tell which stock he belongs to - which is itself the finding. *** /name/ separates an Italian Lerena/Lerina stock from this family; it has always been able to do that by country, and this act is the case where country does not decide.

*** THE HOUSEHOLD THIS ARCHIVE PUBLISHED AS A TRUE NULL, AND IT WAS NEVER ONE. *** Leandro, born about 1854-57 at SEGOVIA, an oil maker, literate; his wife Lucia Llanos; children Emilia (b. Spain c.1886), Francisco (b. La Plata c.1890), Paulina (b. 1895) and, on the baptism of San Cristobal on 20 December 1896, SALVADOR - the son whose army card spells the surname LORENA. Living at Calle Pichincha 929. *** A FOURTH SPANISH ARRIVAL beside the three the Spain lane already draws, and NOT SHOWN TO BE CONNECTED TO ANY OF THEM. *** Segovia is also outside the one Spanish cluster this archive can point to - La Rioja, at 39.6 times the national rate - which makes kinship with the Navarrete household less likely, not more.
